title: Request Trace Inspector — UX sketches, interaction notes, and backlog
notes:
Purpose and scope:
- Draft for a compact "Trace Inspector panel" that can sit next to the request detail view in the Console.
- Focus: quick root-cause triage for failures & latency spikes, easy span navigation, and flexible filter combinators for ad-hoc investigation.

Primary user journeys (short):
1) Engineer on-call: open a slow request, jump to the longest spans, correlate with model variant/region, create a follow-up issue.
2) Platform engineer: bulk-filter traces by GPU type and quantization variant to validate rollout impact.
3) Support rep: find traces for a customer session, redact, and attach to support ticket.

Key UX constraints and principles:
- Keep timeline context visible (request start/end + model response token stream if available).
- Progressive disclosure: show summary row for spans, expand for headers and metadata only when needed.
- Keyboard-first navigation: left/right to move across spans, up/down to jump across parent/child levels.
- Avoid overwhelming users: default to aggregated span groups for high-span-count traces (>200 spans).
- Fast filters: typing a filter should start updating the waterfall after 200ms debounce; spinner only after 500ms.

Wireframe notes (low-fi, non-visual descriptions):
- Left column: Trace summary card (ID, status, duration, model, region, env tag). Small actions: copy-id, pin-to-issue, open raw trace JSON.
- Middle: Waterfall canvas with time ruler (ms) and span rows. Each row shows: span name, duration bar, status badge, model-version pill, device icon. Hover shows quick tooltip with start/finish timestamps + top 3 attributes. Clicking span opens right-side details.
- Right column: Span detail panel with tabs: Overview | Logs & Events | Metadata | Related Traces. Top of panel shows breadcrumbs (Trace > parent span > selected span).
- Compact mode: collapses left and right columns leaving full-width waterfall (for debugging on smaller screens).

Interaction patterns and microcopy:
- Span grouping: "Group similar spans" toggle. Default OFF. When ON, spans with identical opName+attributes collapse into a single expandable group.
- Filter grammar (proposed): attribute op value, operators: =, !=, ~ (regex), in:[]; examples: device=gpu-v100, status!=ok, model~".*-quant". Support parentheses for AND/OR precedence.
- Quick filters (chips) above waterfall: latency > 200ms, errors only, model:rwkv-3, device:gpu. Clicking chip toggles it.
- Keyboard nav: Enter to expand span, Shift+Enter to open full details panel, / to focus filter input, ? for keyboard help overlay.

Data mapping notes (for engineering):
- Trace model fields required to support UI: trace_id, span_id, parent_id, op_name, start_time_ns, duration_ns, status_code, attributes{key->value}, events[], resource{region,device,model_version}, sampled_stack_trace (optional).
- Waterfall timeline should use start_time relative to trace start. Ruler tick marks at dynamic intervals: auto choose 5/10/50/100ms based on total duration.

Accessibility and performance considerations:
- All interactive items must be reachable by tab and have aria-labels.
- Color-blind safe palette for status and device icons.
- Large traces: render virtualization (windowing) for span rows to keep memory under control.
- Telemetry: fire events for filter applied, span expanded, pin-to-issue, and export-trace. Include trace_id and user_role in the event payload.

Open questions / unresolved decisions (notes to self):
- Should span grouping be on by default for traces > 100 spans? Pros: less noise. Cons: can hide important variance.
- How to show token-stream alignment for streaming responses? Option A: overlay token swimlane above waterfall. Option B: inline small token markers on span bars. Need more PM/product input.
- Backlinking: create 'open in APM' link if trace exists in external APM -- how to surface auth?

Backlog grooming list (sprint buckets and rough sizes):
- (M) UX: Compact/expanded layout toggle + keyboard shortcuts — 3pts — [AC: toggle persists per-user].
- (L) Core: Waterfall rendering + virtualization + time-ruler — 8pts — [AC: <200ms initial render for 500-span trace sample].
- (S) Core: Basic filter input + quick chips + debounce behavior — 3pts — [AC: filters applied client-side for traces already loaded].
- (M) Eng: Span grouping algorithm & UI — 5pts — [AC: grouping preserves span order, shows collapsed count].
- (S) Product: Quick export (JSON, link-to-issue) — 2pts — [AC: exported JSON includes selected span context].
- (M) Security: Redaction helper for support — 3pts — [AC: redact attributes with pii tag before export].
- (L) Integrations: model variant and infra filters (cloud regions, gpu type) — 8pts — [AC: can filter by resource tags and show counts].

Acceptance criteria / Examples of done for top ticket (Waterfall rendering):
- Waterfall shows spans in time order and nested hierarchy.
- Start/duration bars align to a shared time scale and match golden dataset (provide sample trace id RINF-DEMO-0001).
- Expand/collapse of parent spans preserves horizontal scrolling position.
- Unit tests for timeline scale calculations and virtualization boundaries.

Notes on grooming decisions:
- Prioritize fast-rendering and keyboard navigation before fancy visual polish.
- Ship minimal filter grammar first (exact match + existence + simple range) and iterate.

Related artifacts and references:
- Recent playtests: internal session notes (2024-09-18) showed keyboard users prefer compact view.
- Bench dataset: trace-samples/wide-span-distribution-2024.json (for perf testing).

- @Priya: draft filter grammar docs and initial parser spec (due 2024-10-28).
- @Tom: prepare conformance checklist for telemetry & PII redaction (due 2024-11-01).

Quick ideas to consider later (parking lot):

- Link spans to failed model evals (if we can match run_id attribute).
- Saved investigations: ability to save a set of filters + selected spans as a permalink for mobile support follow-ups.
